collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager who was never the best at anything shells beans in the evening sun and finds an ordinary life holds a lot.

setup.name: The scene
setup.text: (name1) has never been the best at anything. Not the best fisher, not the best builder, not the best cook, not the best singer. There are no songs about (him/her) and no carvings. When (he/she) was young, that bothered (him/her) a great deal. Today, sitting on (his/her) doorstep shelling beans in the evening sun, with neighbors calling hello as they pass, a child asleep on the mat nearby after being read the same story four times, and a pot of something (he/she) made bubbling gently on the fire, (name1) realizes (he/she) hasn't thought about being the best at anything for years. (He/she) has been too busy living. (He/she) shells another bean, and another, and finds that a very ordinary life, looked at closely, has a lot in it.
